newsitem.title: FINLAND: Benefon sees continuing price pressure.
newsitem.headline: Benefon sees continuing price pressure.

text.p: Finnish mobile phones maker Benefon Oy said on Friday price pressures would continue and require increased efficiency, and repeated it had not yet won type approval for its first digital GSM product.

"Price pressure in the markets will continue this year setting high standards ... in reducing unit costs of the products and in achieving sufficient operational efficiency," Benefon said in a statement with its 1996 results.
"The finishing of the first GSM product ... proceeded slower than intended and ... the final type approval process could not be finished by the end of (1996)," it said.
Benefon said it would continue "intensive long-term efforts to develop the needed world class systems capabilities in all central functions together with needed new products and markets."
It said its strong financial position povided a good base for this effort.

The global trend in the handset market -- a "shift ever more clearly into digital services and especially into GSM-based services" -- underlined the urgency for Benefon to receive type approval for its GSM (Global System fort Mobile Communication) phone.

On Wednesday, Benefon CEO Jorma Nieminen told Reuters no time frame could be given for the approval, although it was close. "As we have indicated earlier, we are close to the type approval, but we don't know when it will be granted," he said.
The company's full-year 1996 net sales fell slightly although the production volume "increased substantially reflecting the falling average prices," Benefon said.
Net sales fell to 284 million markka from 301 million with exports accounting for 94 percent.
Profit before extraordinary items and tax fell to 32 million markka from 74 million.
